chunks: He said: Abu Hafs, Umar ibn Muhammad ibn Ali al-Sayrafi, reported to me from Ja'far ibn Muhammad al-Hasani, who reported from Isa ibn Mihran, who reported from Yunus ibn Muhammad, who reported from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Ghasil, who reported from Abd al-Rahman ibn Khallad al-Ansari, from Ikrimah, from Abdullah ibn Abbas who said:

Ali ibn Abi Talib, al-Abbas ibn Abd al-Muttalib, and al-Fadhl ibn al-Abbas entered upon the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his family and grant them peace, during his illness in which he passed away. They said: 'O Messenger of God, the Ansar are in the mosque, their men and women weeping over you.' He said: 'What makes them weep?' They said: 'They fear you might die.' He said: 'Give me your hands.' So he went out wrapped in a blanket and headband until he sat upon the pulpit. He praised God and glorified His name, then said:

'O people, what makes you feel unusual about your Prophet's death? Have I not announced death to you, and have you not announced deaths among yourselves? If anyone before me had been made eternal and then the angel of death had been sent to him, I would have remained among you. Behold, I am going to meet my Lord, and I have left among you something which, if you hold fast to it, you will never go astray: the Book of God the Exalted, in your midst, which you recite morning and evening. So do not be rivals, do not envy one another, do not harbour enmity, and be brothers as God has commanded you. And I have left among you my progeny, my Ahl al-Bayt, and I enjoin you about them.

Then I enjoin you about this tribe of the Ansar, for you know their sacrifice in the sight of God, Mighty and Majestic, and in the sight of His Messenger and the believers. Did they not widen their homes, share equally their fruits, and prefer others over themselves though they were afflicted with poverty? So whoever among you is given authority in a matter that could harm or benefit anyone, let him accept from the righteous of the Ansar and forgive their wrongdoers.' And this was the last assembly in which he sat before he met God, Mighty and Majestic.

key_terms.أهل بيتي: My household (Ahl al-Bayt) — the Prophet's family, rightful successors and interpreters of Islam
key_terms.الأنصار: The Ansar (Helpers) — Muslims of Medina who sheltered the Prophet and emigrants from Mecca
key_terms.الخصاصة: Poverty/need — the selfless generosity of the Ansar despite their own deprivation
key_terms.عترتي: My progeny (itrati) — the Prophet's household (Ahl al-Bayt), central to Shia theology as guides after the Prophet
key_terms.كتاب الله: The Book of God — the Quran, one of the two weighty things (thaqalayn)

ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet Muhammad say in his last assembly before his death?
ai.summary: This hadith records the Prophet Muhammad's (SAWW) final public address delivered from the pulpit shortly before his death, despite severe illness. He consoled the weeping Ansar, reminded the people that death is inevitable for all prophets, and left two weighty legacies: the Book of God and his progeny (Ahl al-Bayt). He urged the community to avoid rivalry, envy, and hatred, to remain brothers, and commended the Ansar for their extraordinary sacrifices in sheltering the Muslim emigrants.

en.mulla-asgharali-m-m-jaffer: 6. He said: Abu Hafs, Umar ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Ali al-Sayrafl, reported to me from Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Hasani, who reported from Isa ibn Mehran, who reported from Yunus ibn Muhammad, who reported from Abdul Rahman Ibn al-Ghaseel, who reported from Abdul Rahman ibn Khallad al-Ansari, from Ikrarmah, from Abdullah ibn Abbas who said:

‘Ali ibn Abi Talib (as), al-Abbas ibn Abdul Muttalib and al-Fadhl ibn al-Abbas called upon the Prophet, peace be upon him and his progeny, in the last days of his illness, and said: "O messenger of Allah, these Ansar have gathered in the mosque, ladies and men, weeping over you." He asked: "What makes them weep?" They said: "They fear you might die." He said: "Hold me by your hands," then he came out, wrapped in his blanket and headcloth and sat on the pulpit. He thanked Allah and glorified His name, and then said:

"O people, what makes you feel unusual about your Prophet’s death? Have I not announced death to you and have you not announced deaths among your own people? If there had been someone before me, and then the angel of death had come to him later, I would have also remained with you for that long. Be it known that I am going to meet my Sustainer, and I have left among you something, if you adhere to it, you will not be lost. The Book of Allah is with you, read it at dawn and dusk. And do not be each others’ rivals, nor envious, not harbour any enmity against each other. Remain brothers as commanded by Allah. And then I have left behind my family, my Ahlul Bayt, and I enjoy upon you about them.

And then I enjoy upon you about these people of Ansar, whose hardship for the sake of Allah, His Prophet and the believers are known to you. Did they not widen their houses and distribute equally their fruits? Did they not prefer others above themselves, though they were afflicted with poverty? So, whoever from among you is given any worthwhile authority, enabling him to harm or benefit, he should accept the righteous men from Ansar, and also forgive their evil-doers." This was the last assembly in which he sat before he met with his Lord.
